items.title: Neoadjuvant short-course radiotherapy followed by camrelizumab and chemotherapy versus standard of care for locally advanced rectal cancer (UNION): a prespecified interim analysis of a multicentre, open-label, randomised, phase 3 trial.
items.abstract:
BACKGROUND: To our knowledge, UNION is the first phase 3 trial to assess a neoadjuvant strategy incorporating radiotherapy, immunotherapy, and chemotherapy compared with standard care in patients with locally advanced rectal cancer, which reported positive results for the primary endpoint (blinded independent review committee [BIRC]-assessed pathological complete response rate; 39·8% vs 15·3%). Here, we present a prespecified interim analysis of event-free survival.
METHODS: This open-label, randomised, phase 3 trial was conducted at nine hospitals in China. Eligible patients were aged 18-75 years with untreated cT3-4 or N+ rectal adenocarcinoma (≤10 cm distance from the anal verge) and an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status of 0 or 1. Patients were randomly assigned (1:1; stratified by clinical T stage and N stage), using permuted blocks, to receive neoadjuvant short-course radiotherapy (25 Gy in five fractions) followed by two cycles of intravenous camrelizumab (200 mg on day 1) plus CAPOX (oral capecitabine 1000 mg/m2 twice daily on days 1-14 and intravenous oxaliplatin 130 mg/m2 on day 1; experimental group) or long-course chemoradiotherapy (50·4 Gy in 28 fractions with concurrent oral capecitabine 825 mg/m2 twice daily) followed by two cycles of CAPOX (standard-of-care group). After surgery, both groups received six cycles of adjuvant CAPOX, and the experimental group additionally received adjuvant camrelizumab for up to 15 cycles. The primary endpoint was BIRC-assessed pathological complete response rate in the intention-to-treat population, which has been previously reported. Here, we performed a prespecified interim analysis of investigator-assessed event-free survival (one of the key secondary endpoints, defined as time from randomisation to radiographic progression precluding surgery, local recurrence or distant metastasis, or death) in the intention-to-treat population (all randomly assigned patients) with a boundary of a two-sided p values less than 0·0102. Safety was evaluated in all patients who received at least one dose of the study treatment according to the assigned regimen. The study was registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT04928807, and is active, but no longer recruiting.
FINDINGS: Between July 23, 2021, and March 1, 2023, 231 patients (153 [66%] males and 78 [34%] females; 227 [98%] were Han Chinese, and four [2%] were other ethnicity Chinese) were randomly assigned to the experimental group (n=113) and standard-of-care group (n=118). As of Oct 1, 2025, the median follow-up duration was 36·7 months (IQR 32·6-39·9) in the experimental group and 34·7 months (31·1-39·1) in the standard-of-care group. The 3-year investigator-assessed event-free survival rate was 91·3% (95% CI 83·9-95·4) in the experimental group versus 77·4% (67·9-84·4) in the standard-of-care group (stratified hazard ratio 0·33 [0·15-0·71]; two-sided log-rank p=0·0029). During the entire treatment period, the most common grade 3 or 4 treatment-related adverse events were decreased lymphocyte count (23 [20%] of 115 in the experimental group vs 31 [28%] of 112 in the standard-of-care group), decreased white blood cell count (13 [11%] vs 16 [14%]), decreased neutrophil count (13 [11%] vs 13 [12%]), and decreased platelet count (seven [6%] vs 15 [13%]). Treatment-related serious adverse events occurred in 22 (19%) versus 15 (13%) patients, with the most common being decreased platelet count (one [1%] vs six [5%]), and radiation gastroenteritis (two [2%] vs four [4%]). Treatment-related deaths occurred in one patient in the experimental group (septic shock related to chemotherapy, but unrelated to camrelizumab) and none in the standard-of-care group.
INTERPRETATION: In this interim analysis, short-course radiotherapy followed by camrelizumab and CAPOX significantly improved 3-year event-free survival in patients with locally advanced rectal cancer, with a safety profile similar to long-course chemoradiotherapy followed by CAPOX. Comparison of this promising new treatment strategy with contemporary total neoadjuvant therapy strategies is warranted.

items.title: Efzofitimod versus placebo in patients with pulmonary sarcoidosis (EFZO-FIT): a multicentre, randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase 3 trial.
items.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Oral corticosteroids are currently standard-of-care therapy for pulmonary sarcoidosis, but they are associated with substantial toxicity and reduced health-related quality of life (HRQoL). The EFZO-FIT trial aimed to assess the efficacy and safety of efzofitimod, a novel immunomodulatory fusion protein targeting the neuropilin 2 receptor, as a steroid-sparing agent in pulmonary sarcoidosis.
METHODS: In this multicentre, randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase 3 trial, adults aged 18-75 years with pulmonary sarcoidosis requiring treatment were enrolled at 85 study centres across nine countries (Brazil, France, Germany, Italy, Japan, Netherlands, Spain, UK, and USA). Participants were randomly assigned 1:1:1 using stratified block randomisation to receive monthly intravenous infusions of efzofitimod 3 mg/kg, efzofitimod 5 mg/kg, or placebo over a 48-week treatment period, including a 12-week oral corticosteroid taper targeting 0 mg per day (starting on day 15). Oral corticosteroid dose could be adjusted upwards in the event of worsening sarcoidosis. The primary endpoint was change from baseline in mean daily oral corticosteroid dose at week 48. Outcome and safety analyses were done in participants who received at least one dose of the study drug and had at least one post-baseline efficacy assessment. This study was registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05415137) and is complete.
FINDINGS: Between Sept 22, 2022, and Aug 14, 2025, 331 patients were screened for inclusion. 63 were excluded and 268 participants were randomly assigned to receive placebo (n=91), efzofitimod 3 mg/kg (n=89), or efzofitimod 5 mg/kg (n=88). Four patients were excluded after random assignment (one in the placebo group and three in the efzofitimod 3 mg/kg group). 264 patients who received at least one dose of study treatment and had at least one post-baseline assessment were included in the outcome analysis and safety population (90 in the placebo group, 86 in the efzofitimod 3 mg/kg group, and 88 in the efzofitimod 5 mg/kg group). Among the 264 participants, the mean age was 53·8 years (SD 10·6); 114 (43%) of 264 patients were female and 150 (57%) were male. 168 (64%) identified as White. Mean steroid dose was 10·7 mg per day (SD 4·4) at baseline and 2·9 mg per day (4·5) at week 48. No difference was seen in the magnitude of oral corticosteroid taper between the active and placebo dose groups; the placebo-adjusted change from baseline was 0·02 mg per day in the efzofitimod 3 mg/kg group (95% CI -1·49 to 1·52, p=0·98) and -0·73 mg per day in the efzofitimod 5 mg/kg group (-2·21 to 0·75, p=0·33). The percentage of participants with serious treatment-emergent adverse events was similar between groups. Malaise was more common in the placebo group (five [6%] of 90 patients vs zero in both efzofitimod groups). TEAEs that were more common in the efzofitimod groups included headache (17 [19%] of 88 patients in the efzofitimod 5 mg/kg group, 11 [13%] of 86 patients in the efzofitimod 3 mg/kg group, and four [4%] of 90 patients in the placebo group), sinusitis (nine [10%], six [7%], and two [2%] patients, respectively), wheezing (seven [8%], two [2%], and zero patients, respectively), and aspartate aminotransferase (AST) increased (five [6%], one [1%], and zero patients, respectively). Most adverse events were grade 1 or 2. Two participants died, both in the efzofitimod 3 mg/kg group (one respiratory failure and one incarceration of a pre-existing inguinal hernia). Neither event was considered to be causally related to the treatment.
INTERPRETATION: Efzofitimod was well tolerated but did not result in lower steroid doses at week 48 compared with placebo. The results from steroid tapering indicate that oral corticosteroid doses can be more aggressively reduced in many patients with pulmonary sarcoidosis.
FUNDING: aTyr and Kyorin.

items.title: Single Intranasal Administration of the Psychedelic Mebufotenin for Treatment-Resistant Depression: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
items.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Psychedelics represent a potential breakthrough for treatment-resistant depression; however, the prolonged in-clinic monitoring required for compounds such as psilocybin and lysergic acid diethylamide is a logistical hurdle to widespread use. Intranasal mebufotenin (5-methoxy-N,N-dimethyltryptamine), a 5-hydroxytryptamine 1A (5-HT1A) and 5-HT2A agonist associated with brief psychedelic experiences, may address this limitation.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the safety, efficacy, and time to discharge readiness following a single dose of intranasal mebufotenin benzoate in adults with treatment-resistant depression.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: Phase 2b, randomized, double-blind trial with an 8-week blinded follow-up conducted between September 2023 and April 2025 at 38 sites in Australia, Europe, and the US. Participants were aged 18 to 75 years with moderate to severe major depressive disorder nonresponsive to 2 to 5 antidepressant trials in the current episode. The last date of follow-up was April 28, 2025.
INTERVENTIONS: After antidepressant washout as needed, participants were randomly assigned to receive a single dose of intranasal mebufotenin benzoate, 8 mg (n = 46), 12 mg (n = 73), or 0.3 mg (a low-dose comparator; n = 74), alongside psychological support.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary end point was total score change on the Montgomery-Åsberg Depression Rating Scale (MADRS; score range, 0-60; higher scores indicate more severe depression) from baseline to day 29 in the 12-mg vs 0.3-mg dose groups. Eighteen secondary end points were assessed for the 12-mg and 8-mg vs 0.3-mg doses. Discharge readiness was assessed starting 90 minutes after dosing.
RESULTS: Among the 193 included participants, the mean age was 41 (SD, 11.1) years and 59.1% were female. items.title: Permissive Blood Pressure Targets in Pediatric Critical Care: The PRESSURE Randomized Clinical Trial.
items.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Vasoactive drugs are often given to critically ill children to treat hypotension. However, optimal mean arterial pressure (MAP) targets are unknown.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate whether adopting a permissive MAP target, and thereby potentially reducing exposure to vasoactive drugs, improves outcomes in hypotensive critically ill children.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This multicenter, unblinded, pragmatic randomized clinical trial was conducted in 23 pediatric intensive care units (PICUs) in 3 countries. Critically ill children receiving invasive ventilation and vasoactive drugs for hypotension were enrolled between November 2021 and May 2026. Follow-up to the 30-day outcome was completed in June 2026.
INTERVENTIONS: Patients randomized to the intervention (n = 957) were assigned a permissive MAP target greater than the fifth percentile for age. Patients in the control group (n = 943) received usual care with MAP target set by the attending physician.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcome was a composite of mortality and duration of invasive ventilation at 30 days. Secondary outcomes included mortality at PICU discharge, time to cessation of invasive ventilation, receipt and duration of kidney replacement therapy in PICU at 30 days, and length of PICU and hospital stay.
RESULTS: Of 1900 randomized patients, 910 in the permissive MAP target group and 904 in the usual care group were included for analysis of the primary outcome. Participants had a median (IQR) age of 4 (0-10) years and 44.8% were female; baseline characteristics were similar between the groups. Median (IQR) MAP while receiving vasoactive drugs was 58 (51-63) mm Hg in the permissive MAP target group and 61 (54-67) mm Hg in the usual care group. A permissive MAP target led to a 37.5% reduction in median norepinephrine-equivalent total dose compared with the usual care group. There was no significant difference between the groups in the primary outcome (probabilistic index, 0.52 [95% CI, 0.49-0.54]; P = .23). Six of the 7 secondary outcomes were similar between the groups, except median (IQR) PICU length of stay was significantly shorter in survivors in the permissive MAP target vs usual care group (159 [79-286] vs 166 [92-319] hours); probabilistic index, 0.53 [95% CI, 0.50-0.56]). Receipt of kidney replacement therapy and adverse events did not differ between the groups.
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Adopting a permissive MAP target resulted in no significant difference in mortality and duration of invasive ventilation at 30 days compared with usual care.

UBT251 significantly reduced fasting blood glucose, 2-h postprandial glucose, and waist circumference versus placebo (all p < 0.001). Weight reduction with UBT251 was significantly greater than both placebo and semaglutide (all p < 0.05). Gastrointestinal events were the most common treatment-emergent adverse events. These findings support further phase 3 evaluation of UBT251. Registration: CTR20250029; NCT07163624.

items.title: Preoperative Intranasal Oxytocin and Probable Acute Stress Disorder After Traumatic Fracture Surgery: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
items.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Acute stress disorder (ASD) is a common and debilitating psychological sequela following traumatic fracture surgery, adversely affecting recovery and predicting chronic posttraumatic stress disorder. Effective pharmacological prevention strategies are currently lacking.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of a single preoperative dose of intranasal oxytocin for the prevention of screening-positive probable ASD in patients undergoing traumatic fracture surgery.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This single-center, prospective, double-blind, placebo-controlled randomized clinical trial was conducted at the General Hospital of Western Theater Command in China. From April 2024 to April 2025, adult patients scheduled for traumatic fracture surgery were enrolled and randomized.
INTERVENTIONS: Participants were randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to either receive intranasal oxytocin, 40 IU, or an equivalent volume of intranasal saline placebo 10 minutes before the induction of anesthesia.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcome was the cumulative incidence of a first screening-positive probable ASD within 3 days postoperatively, defined by a Stanford Acute Stress Reaction Questionnaire (SAS-RQ) score of 40 or higher. Key secondary outcomes included the Connor-Davidson Resilience Scale (CD-RISC), the Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale (HADS), and salivary malondialdehyde, cortisol, and superoxide dismutase levels.
RESULTS: A total of 328 patients were randomized (164 to the saline group and 164 to the oxytocin group) and included in the intention-to-treat analysis. The median (IQR) age of all participants was 50 (34-57) years; 210 participants (64.0%) were male, and 118 participants (36.0%) were female. The 3-day cumulative incidence of screening-positive probable ASD was 26 of 164 (15.9%) in the oxytocin group vs 50 of 164 (30.5%) in the saline group (risk difference, -14.6 percentage points [pp]; 95% CI, -23.5 to -5.5 pp; risk ratio, 0.52; 95% CI, 0.34-0.79). In the prespecified Cox model, preoperative oxytocin was associated with a lower hazard of a positive screening result during follow-up (adjusted hazard ratio, 0.45; 95% CI, 0.27-0.75). Exploratory analyses suggested improved psychological outcomes and directionally consistent alterations in stress biomarker trajectories. No serious adverse events were observed.
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this randomized clinical trial, preoperative intranasal oxytocin is associated with a lower cumulative incidence of probable ASD after traumatic fracture surgery. These findings suggest that intranasal oxytocin may represent a feasible perioperative preventive strategy; however, these exploratory mechanistic insights and long-term safety profile warrant further investigation.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: Chinese Clinical Trial Registry Identifier: ChiCTR2400082612.

items.title: Intrauterine Mepivacaine Instillation vs Placebo for Pain During IUD Placement: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
items.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Concern about pain during intrauterine device (IUD) placement is common and reduces selection of an IUD. Reducing procedure-related pain may support informed contraceptive decision-making and patient autonomy and has also been associated with improved patient satisfaction and procedural experience.
OBJECTIVE: To determine whether intrauterine instillation of mepivacaine reduces pain during IUD placement in nulliparous individuals.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: Multicenter, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial conducted at 11 outpatient gynecology, maternal health, and youth clinics in Sweden from May 2021 through June 2024. Nulliparous individuals aged 18 to 31 years opting for IUDs with smaller-diameter placement tubes (levonorgestrel 19.5 mg, 13.5 mg, or copper IUD) were eligible. Key exclusion criteria included ongoing pregnancy, IUD replacement, pelvic infection, and allergy to local anesthetics. A total of 370 participants were randomized.
INTERVENTIONS: Participants were randomly assigned (1:1) (185 per group) to intrauterine instillation of 10 mL of mepivacaine (20 mg/mL) or sodium chloride (9 mg/mL) via a hydrosonography catheter 2 minutes before IUD placement. Participants, clinicians, and outcome assessors were blinded to treatment allocation.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcome was clinician-adjusted difference in pain scores during IUD placement, measured on a 100-mm visual analog scale. The primary analysis included all randomized participants with available primary outcome data. Prespecified secondary analyses included tolerability and overall experience.
RESULTS: A total of 370 participants were randomized. Mean age was 21.7 (SD, 3.0) years in the mepivacaine group and 21.7 (SD, 2.9) years in the placebo group. Mean pain score during IUD placement was 43.8 mm (SD, 24.7) in the mepivacaine group and 58.6 mm (SD, 21.5) in the placebo group (mean difference, 14.8 mm [95% CI, 10.0-19.6]; P < .001). Adjustment for individual clinician yielded similar results (mean difference, 14.2 mm [95% CI, 9.7-18.6]; P < .001). Tolerable pain was reported by 172 of 175 participants (98.3%) in the mepivacaine group and 159 of 174 (91.4%) in the placebo group (relative risk, 1.08 [95% CI, 1.02-1.13]; NNT, 15 [95% CI, 9-43]).
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Intrauterine instillation of 10 mL of mepivacaine (20 mg/mL) significantly reduced pain and improved tolerability during IUD placement compared with instillation of placebo saline.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: EudraCT Identifier: 2020-002271-36.

items.title: Revascularization in Asymptomatic Carotid Artery Stenosis With Hemodynamic Impairment and Cognitive Outcomes: The CREST-H Substudy of the CREST-2 Randomized Clinical Trial.
items.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Cerebral hemodynamic impairment in patients with asymptomatic internal carotid artery (ICA) stenosis is associated with reduced cognition. It is uncertain whether revascularization might be an effective treatment for cognitive impairment in these patients.
OBJECTIVE: To test whether any cognitive benefit from revascularization of high-grade, asymptomatic ICA stenosis varies based on the degree of baseline cerebral hemodynamic impairment.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This substudy was conducted within a multicenter phase 3 randomized clinical trial. Adults (aged 35-86 years) without dementia with eighth-grade education or higher and unilateral asymptomatic ICA stenosis greater than or equal to 70% were enrolled from January 2018 to July 2024 at 61 sites in North America (last follow-up in July 2025). Of 607 participants screened from 2485 in CREST-2, 392 were enrolled. Magnetic resonance or computed tomographic perfusion imaging tested for baseline hemodynamic impairment defined by delayed time-to-peak (TTP) arrival of intravenous contrast in the hemisphere ipsilateral minus contralateral to the stenotic artery.
INTERVENTION: Carotid revascularization (endarterectomy or stenting) plus intensive medical management (IMM) vs IMM alone.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcome was the difference in composite cognitive z score over 1 year based on 5 cognitive tests. The primary analysis tested for an interaction between treatment group (revascularization vs IMM alone) and degree of baseline hemodynamic impairment among those with reduced baseline cognition (cognitive z score ≤-1.0 SD).
RESULTS: Of 392 participants enrolled (mean age, 71 years; 125 [32%] females), 61 were excluded for missing baseline imaging and 40 for missing cognitive examinations or other covariates, leaving 291 with complete data. Fifty-one had reduced cognition at baseline (25 in the revascularization group and 26 in the IMM alone group). TTP ranged from no interhemispheric TTP delay to a more-than-2-second delay. Mean (SD) cognitive z scores were -1.36 (0.51) at baseline and -1.17 (0.47) at 1 year in the revascularization group and -1.34 (0.83) at baseline and -1.01 (0.97) at 1 year in the IMM alone group. The primary analysis showed no difference in cognition by treatment group over 1 year, adjusting for treatment group × hemodynamic status interaction and other covariates (adjusted difference in cognitive z score, -0.15 SD [95% CI, -0.54 to 0.24]). The interaction was not significant (β estimate = 0.018 [95% CI, -0.025 to 0.061]; P = .40).
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this substudy of a randomized clinical trial, there was no differential effect of revascularization vs IMM alone on cognition over 1 year by cerebral hemodynamic status among those with baseline reduced cognition, suggesting that revascularization does not improve cognitive dysfunction by restoring flow to the brain in chronic asymptomatic carotid stenosis.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT03121209.

items.title: Neoadjuvant durvalumab plus chemotherapy in resectable or borderline resectable non-small-cell lung cancer: the phase 2 MDT-BRIDGE trial.
items.abstract: The phase 2 MDT-BRIDGE study is investigating perioperative durvalumab plus neoadjuvant chemotherapy (AEGEAN regimen) in resectable and borderline resectable non-small-cell lung cancer and chemoradiotherapy (CRT) followed by consolidation durvalumab (PACIFIC regimen) in patients who become unresectable after neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy guided by multidisciplinary team assessments during the neoadjuvant period. The primary endpoint was the overall resection rate (descriptive with no formal hypothesis testing). Secondary endpoints included event-free survival, progression-free survival, pathological complete response rate (resectable patients cohort), circulating tumor DNA clearance between baseline and presurgery/pre-CRT and safety. Overall, 142 patients received neoadjuvant treatment; 64.8% and 35.2% were deemed resectable and borderline resectable at baseline, respectively. The overall resection rate (95% confidence interval) was 74.6% (66.7‒81.6) in a population that included more than one-third of patients with borderline resectable disease. R0 resection rate was 96.2% (90.6‒99.0) in those who underwent surgery. Overall, 131 (92.3%) patients had surgery (n = 106) or CRT (n = 25) after neoadjuvant treatment, and 117 (82.4%) patients received adjuvant (n = 94) or consolidation (n = 23) durvalumab. During adjuvant or consolidation durvalumab, maximum grade 3/4 adverse events occurred in 7.4% of resected patients and 17.4% of CRT-treated patients, with 8.5% and 13.0% discontinuing treatment due to adverse events. This multidisciplinary team-guided approach was feasible and enabled delivery of curative-intent treatment (surgery or CRT), followed by durvalumab in most patients, and demonstrated encouraging preliminary efficacy with a manageable adjuvant or consolidation safety profile that was consistent with prior studies. ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT05925530 .

items.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Functional seizures (FS) are a common and disabling presentation in neurology clinics, but evidence-based treatments are difficult to access in Australia and in many regions globally. A brief, scalable, internet-delivered intervention could narrow this treatment gap.
OBJECTIVE: To compare a self-guided and a therapist-guided internet-based intervention for FS, each delivered alongside standard care, with standard care alone.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This was a 3-arm, parallel, randomized clinical trial conducted between February 2022 and April 2024, with follow-up through to 12 months after randomization. The location was a specialist outpatient clinic in Melbourne, Australia. Included were adults (≥18 years) with a documented diagnosis of FS confirmed by video electroencephalogram monitoring and at least 4 seizures per month, excluding comorbid active epilepsy.
INTERVENTIONS: Participants were randomized 1:1:1 to a self-guided internet-based intervention plus standard care, therapist-guided internet-based intervention plus standard care, or standard care alone. Re-PROGRAM is an internet-based intervention developed for FS, comprising 5 structured sessions integrating lifestyle factors, seizure management techniques, and elements of cognitive behavioral, acceptance and commitment, and dialectical behavior therapy.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcome was monthly seizure frequency at 6 weeks, 6 months, and 12 months after randomization, recorded by daily prospective seizure diary, with retrospective estimates used for incomplete records. Secondary outcomes included depression, anxiety, quality of life, psychosocial functioning, and somatic symptoms.
RESULTS: Of 220 individuals screened for eligibility, 107 (mean [SD] age 36.0 [12.4] years; 89 female [83%]) were randomized. Of these participants, 96 contributed to the full analysis set (29 self-guided, 34 therapist-guided, 33 standard care). The self-guided arm produced significantly greater overall reductions in monthly seizure frequency than standard care (rate ratio [RR], 0.35; 95% CI, 0.18-0.69; Holm-Bonferroni [HB] method P = .006), with sustained between-group effects at 6 weeks (RR, 0.37; 95% CI, 0.18-0.76; HB P = .02), 6 months (RR, 0.31; 95% CI, 0.12-0.78; HB P = .04), and 12 months (RR, 0.35; 95% CI, 0.16-0.78; HB P = .03). The self-guided arm also showed greater improvements in anxiety than standard care at all 3 time points and in depression and mental quality of life at 1 or more time points. The therapist-guided arm showed greater improvement in anxiety at 6 months, but reductions in seizure frequency did not reach statistical significance. Direct comparison between the 2 active arms showed no significant difference in seizure reduction (RR, 0.67; 95% CI, 0.33-1.36). Sensitivity analyses confirmed robustness of the primary findings. No adverse events occurred in any arm.
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Results of this randomized clinical trial show that in adults with FS, a self-guided internet-based intervention reduced seizure frequency and improved anxiety relative to standard care, offering a scalable option for patients unable to access specialist psychological care.

items.title: Laparoscopic Versus Open Liver Resection for Colorectal Liver Metastases : An Individual Participant Data Meta-analysis of Four Randomized Clinical Trials.
items.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Randomized clinical trials (RCTs) have compared laparoscopic liver resection (LLR) and open liver resection (OLR) for colorectal liver metastases (CRLM); however, long-term outcomes and subgroup effects have not been comprehensively evaluated.
PURPOSE: To compare postoperative and long-term oncologic outcomes after LLR versus OLR for CRLM using individual participant data from RCTs.
DATA SOURCES: PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials were searched from database inception through March 2025 for RCTs comparing LLR and OLR for CRLM.
STUDY SELECTION: Eligible studies were RCTs comparing LLR and OLR for CRLM.
DATA EXTRACTION: Individual participant data, including unpublished data, were obtained from trial investigators of all 4 published RCTs.
DATA SYNTHESIS: Analyses used a modified intention-to-treat approach and 1-stage individual participant data meta-analysis (IPDMA) with trial-adjusted regression models and g-computation to estimate standardized treatment effects across outcomes, with 95% CIs obtained by nonparametric bootstrap resampling. Prespecified subgroup analyses assessed heterogeneity of treatment effect for the primary outcome. A total of 761 patients were included (laparoscopic, n = 384; open, n = 377). Postoperative morbidity was lower in patients assigned to laparoscopic surgery compared with open surgery (19% vs. 27%). Among patients who received preoperative systemic therapy, morbidity did not differ between groups (25% vs. 24%). Ninety-day mortality was 1.8% after LLR and 0.8% after OLR. After a median follow-up of 93 months, overall survival and disease-free survival did not differ between groups.
LIMITATION: Analyses were limited to variables available across all studies.
CONCLUSION: In this IPDMA of all published RCTs in the field, LLR for CRLM was associated with lower postoperative morbidity than OLR, with similar long-term oncologic outcomes.
PRIMARY FUNDING SOURCE: None. (PROSPERO: CRD42024502655).

items.title: Revascularization of Asymptomatic Carotid Artery Stenosis: Cognitive Results of the CREST-2 Randomized Trials.
items.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Studies show that asymptomatic carotid artery stenosis is associated with diminished cognition. Whether carotid revascularization leads to cognitive improvement is unclear.
OBJECTIVE: To determine whether carotid revascularization improves cognition.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: Prespecified cognitive secondary outcomes of the CREST-2 randomized clinical trials of patients 35 years or older with 70% or greater asymptomatic carotid stenosis. Enrollment was December 2014 through July 2024, and follow-up ended July 2025. Five cognitive tests were administered before treatment and annually up to 4 years. Cognitive performances from 146 clinical sites were centrally assessed by telephone, blinded to treatment.
INTERVENTIONS: Two trials compared carotid stenting plus intensive medical management (CAS + IMM) with IMM alone and carotid endarterectomy plus IMM (CEA + IMM) with IMM alone.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Five cognitive tests, assessing learning, memory, executive function, attention, and processing speed, administered to all patients, were assessed for unadjusted and adjusted mean z scores using a linear mixed model. The minimal clinically important difference was 0.50 SD between treatment groups. The prespecified primary analysis was the fully adjusted composite z score at 4 years. Secondary analyses assessed the individual tests and at the test intervals.
RESULTS: Among 2366 US study patients, 2165 (91.5%) participated in cognitive assessments, 1078 in the CAS trial (529 CAS + IMM; 549 IMM alone) and 1087 in the CEA trial (543 CEA + IMM; 544 IMM alone); mean age was 70.1 years (SD, 7.7) and 37.8% were female. Following baseline, 4954 test batteries were administered for a mean of 2.24 (SD, 1.09) follow-up years. There were no treatment-related differences in the fully adjusted estimated composite z scores at 4 years for either the CAS trial (CAS + IMM, 0.22 [95% CI, 0.13 to 0.30] vs IMM alone, 0.18 [95% CI, 0.09 to 0.27]; between-group difference, 0.03 [95% CI, -0.09 to 0.15]) or the CEA trial (CEA + IMM, 0.25 [95% CI, 0.17 to 0.33] vs IMM, 0.23 [95% CI, 0.15 to 0.32]; between-group difference, 0.02 [95% CI, -0.09 to 0.14]). There were no significant differences between revascularization plus medical management vs IMM alone for any individual cognitive test.
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In patients with severe asymptomatic carotid artery stenosis, revascularization with either CAS or CEA plus IMM, compared with IMM alone, did not significantly improve cognitive function at up to 4 years of follow-up.

items.title: Vitamin K2 and D3 Supplementation in Patients With Severe Coronary Artery Calcification: The DANCODE Trial.
items.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Coronary artery calcification (CAC) progression is a strong predictor of cardiovascular events. We investigated whether supplementation with vitamin K2 and vitamin D3 reduces CAC progression in patients with severe coronary calcification.
METHODS: In this multicenter, double-blind, placebo-controlled randomized trial, 400 participants with a CAC score ≥400 Agatston units (AU) were randomly assigned to vitamin K2 (720 μg/d) plus vitamin D3 (25 μg/d) or placebo for 24 months. Participants were enrolled from February 2023 to February 2024. Noncontrast cardiac computed tomography was performed at baseline, 12 months, and 24 months. The primary end point was change in CAC score at 24 months. Subgroup analyses by sex and baseline CAC subgroups (400-999 and ≥1000 AU) were performed. Change in plaque composition was assessed in a subset with CAC score <1000 AU who underwent coronary computed tomography angiography at baseline and 24 months.
RESULTS: A total of 398 participants (30% women; median age, 71 years) were included. Median baseline CAC was 903 AU, and 44% had CAC ≥1000 AU. In the intention-to-treat analysis, the mean CAC increase was 196 AU (95% CI, 178-214) with vitamin K2 and D3 and 248 AU (95% CI, 225-271 AU) with placebo (between-group difference, -52 AU [95% CI, -79 to -24]). The treatment effect was consistent across sex and baseline CAC subgroups. In the 143 participants who underwent coronary computed tomography angiography, there were a similar increase in total plaque volume and no change in noncalcified plaque volume between groups; progression of calcified plaque volume was attenuated in the intervention group (between-group difference, -8 mm3 [95% CI, -13 to -2]).
CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with severe CAC, supplementation with vitamin K2 and vitamin D3 reduced progression of CAC over 24 months. The reduction in calcification progression was not associated with an increase in noncalcified plaque volume.

items.title: Effectiveness of Nurse-Coordinated, Digital-Supported Collaborative Care Model in Reducing Hospital Stay and Mortality Among Patients With Heart Failure: TIME-HF Cluster RCT (India).
items.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction causes high mortality and recurrent hospitalizations in India. We evaluated the effectiveness of the collaborative care model in improving days alive and out of the hospital and overall survival.
METHODS: We conducted a parallel-group, cluster-randomized controlled trial involving 1507 adults with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction across 22 centers in India (CTRI/2021/11/037797). Centers were randomized 1:1 to the intervention or usual care. Participants were followed up for 2 years. The intervention included risk stratification, lifestyle and pharmacological optimization, and a nurse-coordinated, mobile health-supported disease management program with self-care education, active follow-up, and continuous outpatient monitoring throughout the study period. The primary outcome was days alive and out of the hospital, and all-cause mortality was assessed as a secondary outcome. Days alive and out of the hospital was analyzed with a one-inflated β model. All-cause mortality was analyzed with Cox proportional hazards models adjusted for the clustered study design.
RESULTS: Among 1507 participants (752 usual care; 755 intervention), the mean age was 61.9 years, and 77.6% were men. All participants except one completed 24 months of follow-up. Most participants (70%) had low educational attainment; 57.3% lived in rural areas; and ischemic heart disease was the predominant cause (77.4%). Baseline characteristics were comparable between the intervention and usual care groups. In the one-inflated β model, the probability of surviving up to 730 days without hospitalization was 34.7% (95% CI, 31.2%-38.1%) in the usual care group and 46.5% (95% CI, 42.6%-49.9%) in the intervention group. Participants in the intervention group had 78% higher odds of achieving a percent days alive and out of the hospital of exactly 1 (730/730 days) compared with those in the usual care group (odds ratio, 1.78 [95% CI, 1.42-2.23]). There were 201 deaths (26.73%) in the usual care group compared with 163 deaths (21.59%) in the intervention group (risk ratio, 0.80 [95% CI, 0.67-0.97]). In the multivariable Cox proportional hazards model, the intervention group had a 22% lower mortality risk than the usual care group (hazard ratio, 0.78 [95% CI, 0.63-0.95]; P=0.028).
CONCLUSIONS: A nurse-coordinated, mobile health-supported collaborative care model for heart failure with reduced ejection fraction in India increased the number of days alive and out of hospital, raised the absolute probability of remaining out of hospital by 11.8 percentage points, and reduced all-cause mortality by 22%.

items.title: In vivo genome-editing therapy for Duchenne muscular dystrophy: Preclinical studies and first-in-human trial.
items.abstract: We report the preclinical and early clinical evaluation of in vivo genome editing for Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD), delivered via a single AAV9 vector. In humanized DMD mice, systemic administration achieved targeted genome editing, partial dystrophin restoration, and improved muscle function. In non-human primates, efficient on-target editing was achieved with no dose-limiting toxicity identified under the conditions tested. In an open-label, dose-escalation, first-in-human clinical trial (NCT06594094), post-treatment muscle biopsies provided early molecular evidence of hfCas12Max-mediated genome editing and detectable dystrophin expression in participants with DMD. However, at the higher dose level (1.0 × 1014 vg/kg), one participant experienced a treatment-related fatal serious adverse event, characterized by marked complement activation and systemic cytokine response shortly after dosing. This work provides initial human proof-of-concept for muscle genome editing while crucially highlighting the critical role of immunologic risks and the narrow therapeutic window of systemic adeno-associated virus (AAV)-CRISPR therapies, underscoring the need to develop safer dosing and immunomodulation strategies.
